Section B
Answer any three questions.
Each question is introduced by stimulus material. In your answer you may refer to this material and/or
to other examples that you have studied.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Define population pyramid.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain two reasons why income may become more unevenly distributed.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Analyse the influences on whether demand for shoes is elastic or inelastic.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Discuss whether or not a mixed economic system will benefit the people who live in that
economy.

text: The shape of Colombia’s population pyramid is changing. The income distribution of this South
American country, however, is not changing significantly. The country has one of the most unequal
income distributions in the world. Some Colombians work in its footwear industry which produces
shoes, sandals and boots. Although footwear is produced in the private sector, Colombia has a
mixed economic system.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Identify the rewards to capital and land.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain two causes of a decrease in enterprise in an economy.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Analyse how changes in conditions of supply can affect a firm’s prices.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Discuss whether or not a rise in a national minimum wage will harm an economy.

text: In recent years, the quantity of Latvia’s factors of production has changed. Since 2008, its capital
has increased and its land has not changed significantly, but its labour force and its enterprise
have decreased. Enterprise and conditions of supply can affect firms’ prices. In 2022, the Latvian
Government increased the country’s national minimum wage (NMW). Its NMW did, however,
remain one of the lowest in the European Union.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Identify two macroeconomic aims of government that may conflict.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain two reasons why a country may have a high population growth rate.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Analyse how a cut in the corporation (corporate income) tax rate can increase economic
growth.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Discuss whether or not a decrease in government spending will reduce inflation.

text: In 2023, India became the country with the largest population. This may affect the government’s
macroeconomic aims. In 2018, the Indian Government cut the country’s corporation (corporate
income) tax rate from 35% to 25%. Between 2019 and 2022, India’s inflation rate averaged 6%.
Some economists suggested that to achieve its central inflation rate target, the government should
cut its spending.

text: Australia has a number of firms that operate in other countries. These multinational companies
(MNCs) provide several benefits for their home country of Australia. The Australian Government
imposes relatively low import tariffs and the country has a floating exchange rate. In recent years,
Australia has experienced an increase in investment and a higher Human Development Index
(HDI) value.
